doc.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996

title: Jazz then and now: music as food, and golf
summary: He compares the evolution of jazz to changing food as nourishment for the mind; light chatter about golf and weather.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: What’s your opinion on where the jazz scene is now as compared to when perhaps in the
Well it would be the same opinion as musicians had in the ‘50s and ‘60s who came up in the ‘20s and ‘30s, you know? You see what I mean? © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

They had, from the ‘20s, well you can go back to say 1910 and start coming up and it started changing there, and then it started getting more sophisticated and more educated with the like Fletcher Henderson, and that came along and then all of a sudden bebop came out and that came for a while and so forth and then another form came, and it’s the same — to me it’s the same as food. I always say food and music are very similar. Food is for nourishment of your body, and music is for nourishment of your mind. Now if we were to stay with the same food forever, say meat and potatoes and that’s it, you know. You’d have meat and potatoes and so forth. But we see how food has changed in the last 50 years as we become more sophisticated. And reach out to more people in various ways. And you’ve got the dietitians, you’ve got this, you’ve got that and so forth. And food is there to supplement the bodies, and the music is doing the same thing to supplement the mind.
That’s great. At 8:30 in the morning.
Oh, listen, I could be playing golf.
How’s your golf game these days?
Well it hasn’t been too good because the weather in Washington this last six months has been unbelievable.
We’re from up north too, so it’s a pleasure to be down here. They’re calling it cold you know, but we can live with that.
What do they know about cold weather?
